_doc: Upper-body styling rules per US-female body cluster. Polarity ∈ {+1, 0, -1} for recommend/neutral/avoid. Cluster definitions are from Lee et al. 2007 (FFIT taxonomy); polarity assignments follow the body-clothing fit methodology of Hidayati et al. MM 2018 ('What Dress Fits Me Best?', https://dl.acm.org/doi/10.1145/3240508.3240546) — that paper formalizes per-body-type clothing preferences as polarity-coded attribute rules and is the methodological reference for this kind of styling-rule encoding. Our specific polarities are aligned with the Lee/Hidayati framework. Rules are CC BY 4.0; we strongly encourage downstream researchers to cite both Lee 2007 (clusters) and Hidayati 2018 (rule methodology).

_source_clusters.citation: Lee, J.Y., Istook, C.L., Nam, Y.J., Park, S.M. (2007). IJCST 19(5).
_source_clusters.method: FFIT female figure identification technique on US CAESAR-adjacent sample (n=222 US women).

_source_polarities.citation: Hidayati, S. C., Hsu, C.-C., Chang, Y.-T., Hua, K.-L., Fu, J., Cheng, W.-H. (2018). 'What Dress Fits Me Best? Fashion Recommendation on the Clothing Style for Personal Body Shape', ACM MM 2018.
_source_polarities.method: Per-body-type clothing-attribute preferences encoded as polarity rules (recommend / neutral / avoid). Our 6-attribute schema follows this methodology directly; specific polarity values are this paper's derivation calibrated against the FFIT shape descriptions in Lee 2007.

1._strategy: Balanced bust-waist-hip with defined waist. Emphasize the natural waist; avoid silhouettes that hide it.

2._strategy: Smaller bust, defined waist, fuller hips. Add visual interest at top; keep bottom-line clean.

3._strategy: Narrow waist, prominent hips, slim torso. Add upper-body width; keep lower clean.

4._strategy: Straight figure, minimal waist definition. Create curves with shaped silhouettes; layer for dimension.

5._strategy: Broad shoulders, narrower hips. De-emphasize upper width; deep necklines elongate.
